To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of urea at sowing or in split applications of 50-50-100 kg of N/ha, 50-50 kg of N/100 kg of N at 50 and 100 DAS, and 100-100 kg N at 50-100 DAS to five BWL resulted in significant differences in PC, PSD, and PDP.

Split applications of urea (100-100- 100 or 50-50- 50 kg of urea per hectare) resulted in higher bread loaf volume in comparison to the same amount of nitrogen applied at sowing or as one split application of 300-kg of urea per ha.
split applications of ureaN (100-100-150, 50-50-150, and 50-150-50 kg of urea ha-1) improved bread loaf volume in comparison to the same amount of N applied at sowing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of NF on PSD, PDP and baking performance of wheat lines.
the development of a better understanding of the effect of NF treatment and BWl on PSD, PDP and bread baking performance.
the effect of NF on PSD and PDP of BWL, which are important factors for the baking performance of the wheat flour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the split application of urea (100-100-0, 100-100 kg, 100-50 kg, 100 kg, or 50 kg/ha) to BWL resulted in a better loaf volume performance compared to the application of the same amount of fertilizer at sowing (0-0-0 or 0 kg/ha).
the split application of nitrogen fertilizer to bread wheat is a good management practice to improve the baking performance of wheat cultivars.
the application of urea at sowing or in split applications of 50-50- 50 kg of urea per hectare resulted in the best loaf volume response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of split fertilization of urea at 100-100 kg/ha to BWL 3, 4, and 5 would be the best option to increase the protein content and to improve PDP and baking performance of bread wheat.
the NF treatments modified the PSD and PDP of the BWL.
the application of 300 and 150 kg of Urea/ha at sowing and three split applications of uree, respectively, resulted in higher FUPP and bread loaf volume than the same amount applied at sowing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application of urea at three split applications (50-50 kg of urea per application) to all BW resulted in a higher loaf volume in comparison with the same amount of nitrogen applied at sowing or three applications of 100-50 kg of nitrogen.
the split applications of ureaN (50-50) and (100-100) to the BWL resulted in higher PC and TUPP.
the split application of nitrogen fertilizer at the sowing time, and during the vegetative and reproductive growth stages, can modify the PSD and the PDP of wheat flour.
